mainTopic: Bringing the קרבן פסח when part of the people is טמא: splitting the community, creating a majority, and when פסח שני applies
overview: This amud deals with bringing the קרבן פסח when part of the Jewish people is טמא. It finishes a ברייתא: רבי אלעזר בן מתיא's פסוק, then רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה, who both agree that one שבט counts as a קהל. רבי שמעון lets the pure and the impure each bring their own פסח. רבי יהודה says a קרבן ציבור cannot be split, so everyone brings it in טומאה. When the people are exactly half pure and half impure, רב says to make one pure person טמא with a שרץ. After several questions, the גמרא explains that רב said this only for someone who holds like both the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה. עולא instead sends one person on a דרך רחוקה, and the גמרא explains why he avoids a שרץ or a מת, using his view that all the festival days are תשלומין of the first day. רב נחמן rejects עולא's plan as impractical. רב then rules that if most of the people are זבין, the minority of טמאי מתים lose both the first פסח and פסח שני, and he defends this against שמואל's challenge from בְּמוֹעֲדוֹ. Finally, רב הונא and רב אדא בר אהבה argue whether there is a make-up for a פסח brought in טומאה. The גמרא rejects tying their argument to דחויה versus הותרה and begins a new explanation that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse: not in any one of your cities
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes quoting the פסוק that רבי אלעזר בן מתיא uses as his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: "You may not sacrifice the פסח offering in any one of your cities."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא quotes a פסוק as the source for the view of רבי אלעזר בן מתיא, which began on the previous amud. The word "באחד" (in one) is the key word he learns from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן מתיא learns from the word "one" that a single individual cannot decide whether the whole community brings the קרבן פסח in טהרה or in טומאה. This verse closes his opinion. The ברייתא then moves on to the next תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: You may not / you are not able
to slaughter (as a sacrifice)
the קרבן פסח
in any one of your gates (cities)

phrases.english: "You may not sacrifice the Pesach offering
phrases.notes: דברים טז:ה

phrases.notes: The lesson here is learned from the word "one."

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא תוּכַל לִזְבֹּחַ אֶת הַפָּסַח בְּאַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא earlier by completing רבי אלעזר בן מתיא's verse.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר בן מתיא's view that one individual cannot decide the community's status of טהרה or טומאה

steps.title: רבי שמעון: each group brings its own פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון rules that if one שבט is טמא and the rest are pure, each group brings the קרבן פסח separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: Even if one tribe is impure and all the other tribes are pure, the pure tribes bring the פסח for themselves, and the impure tribe brings it for itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי שמעון's opinion. If one שבט is טמא, the pure שבטים bring the קרבן פסח in טהרה, and the impure שבט brings its own in טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The surprise is that the impure שבט does not have to wait for פסח שני, even though it is only a small part of the people. That שבט still gets to bring its offering in טומאה, separately from everyone else. The גמרא will ask why next.

keyTerms.meaning: tribe
ritually impure
ritually pure
for themselves (separately)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Even if one tribe is impure
and all the rest of the tribes are pure,
these (the pure) perform it for themselves
phrases.notes: in טהרה

phrases.english: and those (the impure) perform it for themselves.
phrases.notes: in טומאה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next opinion in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One impure שבט brings the קרבן פסח in טומאה, while the pure שבטים bring theirs in טהרה.

steps.title: Why does רבי שמעון rule this way?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind רבי שמעון's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי שמעון's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון lets a minority group bring the קרבן פסח in טומאה. This question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally only a whole community, or its majority, may bring a קרבן in טומאה. One שבט is a minority, so רבי שמעון's ruling needs a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a minority שבט may bring the קרבן פסח in טומאה

steps.title: One tribe counts as a community
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds that a single שבט has the status of a קהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that one tribe is called a "community."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון holds one שבט is called a קהל. A קהל is allowed to bring the קרבן פסח in טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The impure שבט is not treated as a few individuals. It counts as a full community on its own. So the rule that a community may bring a קרבן in טומאה applies to that שבט, even while the other שבטים bring theirs in טהרה.

keyTerms.meaning: he holds (his view is)
is called
community / congregation

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that שבט אחד איקרי קהל is the shared starting point for both רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: He holds: one tribe is called a community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One שבט has the status of a קהל, so it may bring the קרבן פסח in טומאה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: everyone brings it in impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that if one שבט is טמא, all the שבטים bring the קרבן פסח in טומאה, because a קרבן ציבור cannot be divided.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Even if one tribe is impure and all the other tribes are pure, they all perform it in impurity, because a communal offering is not divided.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי יהודה's opinion. In the same case, he says everyone, even the pure שבטים, brings the קרבן פסח in טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה adds a new principle: a קרבן ציבור cannot be split into a pure group and an impure group. If the impure שבט may bring it in טומאה, the whole people must bring it together the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: they shall perform it in impurity
communal offering
divided / split

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even if one tribe is impure
and all the rest of the tribes are pure,
they (all) perform it in impurity,
since a communal offering is not divided.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling that disagrees with רבי שמעון in the same case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If one שבט is טמא, all the שבטים bring the קרבן פסח in טומאה, because a קרבן ציבור is not divided.

steps.title: Explaining רבי יהודה: half and half
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that for רבי יהודה, one impure שבט, being a קהל, makes it as if the people were half pure and half impure, and since the offering cannot be split, all bring it in טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds that one tribe is called a community. So it is like half and half, and a communal offering is not divided, so they all perform it in impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי יהודה reaches his ruling. One impure community stands against one pure community, which counts like half and half. Since the offering cannot be split, everyone brings it in טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה agrees with רבי שמעון that one שבט is a קהל. He disagrees only about whether a קרבן ציבור may be split. Because it may not, the impure community pulls everyone into bringing it in טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: half and half
they perform
all of them

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה disagree about whether one שבט is a קהל. They both say it is. They disagree only about whether a קרבן ציבור may be split between pure and impure groups.
steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים hold שבט אחד איקרי קהל. רבי שמעון lets each group bring its own קרבן פסח (pure in טהרה, impure in טומאה). רבי יהודה says a קרבן ציבור cannot be divided, so everyone brings it in טומאה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds:
one tribe is called a community.
So it becomes for them half and half,
phrases.notes: one impure community against one pure community

phrases.english: and a communal offering is not divided,
so all of them perform it in impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: שֵׁבֶט אֶחָד אִיקְּרִי קָהָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind step 5, building on the principle stated in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי יהודה, one impure שבט creates a half-and-half situation, and an undividable קרבן ציבור is then brought by all in טומאה.

steps.title: רב: if exactly half are impure, make one more impure
steps.stepSummary: A new אמוראic dispute is introduced: when the people are exactly half pure and half impure, רב says to make one pure person טמא with a שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: If the Jewish people were half pure and half impure, רב said: They make one of them impure with a creeping creature.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion between אמוראים about an exact half-and-half split. רב says to make one pure person טמא with a שרץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making one more person טמא turns the impure group into a majority. Then the rule that a majority in טומאה may bring the offering in טומאה applies, and everyone brings it together in טומאה. The word אתמר signals that other אמוראים will give different views.

keyTerms.meaning: it was stated (introduces an אמוראic dispute)
half
they make impure
a creeping creature whose carcass transmits טומאה

steps.whyThisMatters: רב's solution shows that having one clear majority matters so much here that it is worth deliberately making someone טמא.

phrases.english: It was stated:
If the Jewish people were half pure
and half impure,
Rav said:
They make one of them impure with a creeping creature.
phrases.notes: This makes the impure group the majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: הָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מֶחֱצָה טְהוֹרִין וּמֶחֱצָה טְמֵאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא's case of one שבט to an exact half-and-half split, which רבי יהודה's explanation in step 6 also touched on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the people are exactly half pure and half impure, one pure person is made טמא with a שרץ so that the majority is impure.

steps.title: Why not let each group bring its own offering, as רב himself rules?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב's שרץ ruling using another ruling of רב: in a half-and-half case, each group brings its own פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do that? Let the pure people bring the offering by themselves, and the impure people by themselves! After all, רב himself said: these bring it for themselves, and those bring it for themselves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's idea of making a pure person טמא. רב himself said elsewhere that in a half-and-half case, each group simply brings its own קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב cannot hold both rulings at once. If the groups can split, there is no reason to make anyone impure on purpose. The two statements of רב look like they contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: And why? An opening that signals a challenge
By themselves, on their own
These perform for themselves
For surely [he] said. Brings a contradicting source

phrases.english: And why?
Let these (the pure) perform on their own
phrases.notes: Bring the פסח in purity

phrases.english: and those (the impure) on their own
phrases.notes: Bring the פסח in impurity

phrases.english: for surely רב said:
These perform for themselves,
and those perform for themselves!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? נִיעְבְּדוּ הָנֵי לְחוֹדַיְיהוּ וְהָנֵי לְחוֹדַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling from Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling to make one pure person טמא with a שרץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction: רב elsewhere rules that in a half-and-half case each group brings its own offering, so making someone impure is unnecessary

steps.title: The case is where the impure outnumber the pure by one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב's שרץ ruling deals with a special case: the impure are more than the pure by exactly one person.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: What case are we dealing with here? A case where the impure outnumbered the pure by one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the שרץ ruling is not about an exact half-and-half split. It is about a slightly different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the impure group is bigger by just one person. The answer tries to make room for both of רב's rulings by giving each its own case: exact halves means split, and a margin of one means use the שרץ.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here? Narrows the case
Outnumber, exceed
They say. Introduces an anonymous answer

phrases.english: They say:
With what are we dealing here?
Such as where the impure outnumbered
the pure by one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8 by redefining the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's שרץ ruling was about an exact half-and-half split
steps.terutzMaskana: It is about a case where the impure exceed the pure by one

steps.title: If the impure are the majority, all should bring it in impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if the impure are the majority, the rule of רוב applies and everyone brings the פסח in טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the impure are the majority! Let them all bring it in impurity!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If the impure group is bigger, everyone should just bring the offering in טומאה, and no שרץ is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual rule is that when most of the people are טמא, the whole community brings the פסח in טומאה. A majority of even one should be enough, so the special case seems to need no trick at all.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. Introduces a follow-up objection
Majority
All of them in impurity

phrases.english: If so,
they are a majority of impure people!
Let them all perform in impurity!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הָווּ לְהוּ רוּבָּא טְמֵאִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the case defined in Step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The case where the impure exceed the pure by one
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A majority of impure people already means everyone brings the offering in טומאה, so the שרץ is unnecessary

steps.title: רב holds like רבי אלעזר בן מתיא: one person cannot tip the community
steps.stepSummary: רב follows רבי אלעזר בן מתיא, who says a single extra person cannot turn the community into a majority of טמאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי אלעזר בן מתיא, who said: a single individual does not tip the community toward impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a majority of only one does not count here, according to רבי אלעזר בן מתיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this view, a margin of one person is not a real majority for making the whole community bring the offering in טומאה. So the case of 'more by one' is treated like an even split.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא whose view is cited here
A single individual
Tips the balance, decides
The community

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן מַתְיָא,
phrases.english: He holds like רבי אלעזר בן מתיא,
who said:
An individual does not tip
the community toward impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן מַתְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A majority of one makes everyone bring it in טומאה
steps.terutzMaskana: A single individual cannot tip the community, so it counts as half and half

steps.title: The original question comes back
steps.stepSummary: If a margin of one counts as half and half, then רב's own ruling applies again: each group should bring its own offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, our difficulty returns to its place: let these bring it by themselves and those by themselves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the last answer leads straight back to the first question from Step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the case counts as half and half, רב's other ruling says to split the groups. So making a pure person טמא with a שרץ is still unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Our difficulty returns to its place. The question stands again

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is the same question from Step 8. The answer in Steps 9 and 11 went in a circle.

phrases.english: If so,
our difficulty returns to its place:
let these perform on their own
and those on their own!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that Step 11's answer brings back the question of Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The combined answer of Steps 9 and 11
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Treating it as half and half brings back רב's own rule of splitting the groups

steps.title: רב's שרץ ruling is advice for one who holds two other views
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reinterprets רב: the שרץ method is not his own opinion. It is for someone who holds like the תנא קמא and also like רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what רב meant: if there is a תנא who holds like the תנא קמא, who said that in a half-and-half case they do not all bring it in impurity, and who also holds like רבי יהודה, who said a communal offering is not divided, then they make one of them impure with a שרץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up trying to make the שרץ ruling fit רב's own view. It explains the ruling as a conditional statement for a different combination of opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says a half-and-half community cannot all bring it in טומאה. רבי יהודה says the offering cannot be split between two groups. A person who holds both is stuck, so the only way out is to make one pure person טמא and create an impure majority. רב himself holds that the groups split, so there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what he meant. A reinterpretation
The first, anonymous opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
Half and half
A creeping creature whose carcass makes a person impure

steps.whatToRemember: רב's own view: in a half-and-half case, each group brings its own פסח. The שרץ method only applies for someone who holds both like the תנא קמא (no all-in-טומאה at half and half) and like רבי יהודה (a קרבן ציבור is not divided).
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how an אמורא can state a rule as a conditional ('if you hold X and Y') without holding it himself. This removes the contradiction.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what he said:
If there is a tanna
who holds like the first tanna,
who said: half and half
do not all perform in impurity,
and he also holds like רבי יהודה,
who said: a communal offering is not divided
— then they make one of them impure with a creeping creature.
phrases.notes: One of the pure people, to create an impure majority

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after Step 12 showed the earlier answer failed
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the statement as conditional
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שרץ ruling is רב's own practical view
steps.terutzMaskana: It applies only to one who holds like both the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה

steps.title: עולא: send one pure person on a distant journey
steps.stepSummary: עולא gives a different method: send one pure person away on a דרך רחוקה so the impure become the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: And עולא said: they send one of them on a distant journey.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא disagrees with רב's method. Instead of making a pure person טמא, he says to send one pure person far away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone on a דרך רחוקה is not counted with the community bringing the פסח. With him gone, the impure are the majority, and everyone present brings it in טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא
They send away
A distant journey, which exempts one from the first פסח

phrases.english: And עולא said:
They send one of them
on a distant journey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative to רב's שרץ method
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the stuck half-and-half case, send one pure person on a דרך רחוקה to create an impure majority

steps.title: Why not just make him impure with a שרץ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks עולא why he does not use רב's simpler method of a שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them make him impure with a שרץ!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions עולא's method. Making someone טמא with a שרץ seems easier than sending him far away. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both methods reach the same goal: an impure majority. The challenge asks why עולא picked the harder route. Presumably he has a reason to avoid the שרץ.

keyTerms.meaning: And let them make him impure

phrases.english: Let them make him impure with a creeping creature!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's method from Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's method of sending one person on a דרך רחוקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Making him טמא with a שרץ is simpler and achieves the same result

steps.title: Why עולא does not use a שרץ
steps.stepSummary: עולא holds that we slaughter and sprinkle the קרבן פסח for a טמא שרץ, so making someone impure with a שרץ does not move him into the impure group.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: we slaughter and sprinkle the blood for someone who is impure from a שרץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 15. A שרץ will not help עולא, because in his view a טמא שרץ still counts as pure for the קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טומאת שרץ lasts only until nightfall. The person can go to the מקוה and be pure in time to eat the פסח at night. So עולא holds we may offer the קרבן on his behalf, and he stays in the pure group. Touching him with a שרץ therefore does not change the count.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (his opinion is)
We slaughter (the קרבן פסח)
We sprinkle (the blood on the מזבח)
A person impure from touching a creeping creature; the impurity ends at nightfall

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the argument between רב and עולא depends on a separate question: whether a טמא שרץ counts as pure for the קרבן פסח. רב's שרץ method only works if a טמא שרץ counts as impure.

phrases.english: He holds: we slaughter and sprinkle
phrases.notes: Explains עולא's underlying opinion.

phrases.english: for one impure from a creeping creature.
phrases.notes: He can become pure by evening and eat the פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reveals an underlying opinion that makes the suggested method useless
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A שרץ should work for עולא just as it works for רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: For עולא, a טמא שרץ still counts as pure for the פסח, so a שרץ does not shift the majority.

steps.title: Suggestion to make him impure with a corpse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why עולא does not make the person טמא מת, which lasts seven days and would surely put him in the impure group.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them make him impure with a dead body!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another simple method in place of sending someone far away: make him impure with a מת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טומאת מת lasts seven days, so this person could not be pure by the night of the פסח. He would definitely count as טמא, and the impure would become the majority. Why go to the trouble of a דרך רחוקה?

keyTerms.meaning: Let them make him impure
Impurity from a dead body; lasts seven days

phrases.english: Let them make him impure with a corpse!
phrases.notes: A seven-day impurity that would surely count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the שרץ is ruled out, the גמרא suggests a stronger impurity.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's choice of the דרך רחוקה method
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מת makes him impure for seven days, so it would work without sending him away.

steps.title: A corpse would take away his חגיגה
steps.stepSummary: Making him טמא מת would stop him from bringing his חגיגה offering during the festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: You would be pushing him away from his festival offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we do not make him טמא מת, because he would then miss a different מצוה, the חגיגה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who becomes טמא מת on the eve of פסח stays impure for much of the festival. He could not bring the קרבן חגיגה, which everyone brings when coming to the בית המקדש on the יום טוב. We should not cause him to lose a מצוה for no reason.

keyTerms.meaning: You push him away (disqualify him)
The festival שלמים offering brought on יום טוב

phrases.english: You are pushing him away from his festival offering.
phrases.notes: He would be impure during the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a cost that the suggested method carries
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Making him טמא מת is a free and easy solution.
steps.terutzMaskana: It costs him the מצוה of חגיגה.

steps.title: Sending him away also costs him a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that עולא's own method also makes the person lose a מצוה: his קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now too, you are pushing him away from his פסח!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same argument against עולא. Sending a pure person on a דרך רחוקה also makes him miss his פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If losing the חגיגה is a reason to avoid the מת method, then losing the קרבן פסח should also rule out the דרך רחוקה method. Both methods cost the person a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Now too (in this case as well)
His קרבן פסח

phrases.english: Now too,
phrases.notes: Refers to עולא's method of sending him away.

phrases.english: you are pushing him away from his Paschal offering!
phrases.notes: Uses the same wording as step 18.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 18 by applying its own logic to עולא's method.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason given in step 18 for rejecting the מת method
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The דרך רחוקה method also takes away a מצוה, so it is no better.

steps.title: He can still bring it on פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: The person sent away has not lost his פסח completely, because he can bring it on פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is possible that he will do it on the second פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the person sent away can make up his קרבן פסח a month later, on פסח שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone on a דרך רחוקה on the fourteenth of ניסן brings his פסח on the fourteenth of אייר. So his מצוה is only delayed, not lost. The גמרא's assumption is that with a מת, the חגיגה would be lost completely.

keyTerms.meaning: It is possible
Second פסח, a month later, for those who missed the first

phrases.english: It is possible that he will perform it on the second (פסח).
phrases.notes: The fourteenth of אייר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes a delayed מצוה from a lost מצוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sending him away takes away his פסח entirely.
steps.terutzMaskana: His פסח is only delayed until פסח שני.

steps.title: The טמא מת can also make up his חגיגה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the טמא מת can also bring his חגיגה later, on the seventh day of פסח, which is his eighth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a corpse too, it is possible that he will do it on the seventh day, which is his eighth day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the 'only delayed, not lost' logic against the answer of step 18. The טמא מת can also bring his חגיגה before the festival ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he becomes impure on the fourteenth of ניסן, his seven days end on the twentieth. On the twenty-first, his eighth day and the seventh day of פסח, he is pure and can bring the חגיגה. The חגיגה can be made up all seven days, so with a מת he also loses nothing. The next step answers this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh day of פסח
His own eighth day (of the impurity count)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two counts. 'שביעי' is the seventh day of the festival. 'שמיני שלו' is the eighth day of HIS impurity count. It is the same calendar day, the twenty-first of ניסן.

phrases.english: With a corpse too,
phrases.notes: Turns step 20's logic back on step 18.

phrases.english: it is possible that he will perform it on the seventh (day of the festival)
phrases.notes: He brings the חגיגה then.

phrases.english: which is his eighth day!
phrases.notes: By then his seven days of טומאה are over.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses step 20's reasoning to undo step 18's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 18 that a מת takes away his חגיגה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חגיגה can be made up on the seventh day of פסח, so it is only delayed, just like the פסח in step 20.

steps.title: עולא holds that all festival days only make up for the first day
steps.stepSummary: עולא holds that the later days of the festival are תשלומין of the first day. So someone unfit on the first day cannot bring his חגיגה on any later day.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא holds: all the days are make-up days for the first day. Whoever is fit on the first day is fit on all of them. Whoever is not fit on the first day is not fit on any of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 21. A טמא מת cannot bring his חגיגה later in the festival, because he was not fit on the first day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 claimed that a טמא מת could bring his חגיגה on the seventh day, which is his eighth day. This answer explains that the later days are not separate chances. They only 'make up' for day one, so a person who was never obligated-and-fit on day one has nothing to make up. That is why עולא could not make the person a טמא מת: he would lose his חגיגה completely.

keyTerms.meaning: Make-up days; later chances to fulfill an obligation from an earlier day
Of the first (day of the festival)
Is fit / eligible
All of them (all the festival days)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the later days of the festival are independent days for bringing the חגיגה. According to עולא, they are only extensions of day one. If you were not fit on day one, the later days do not help you.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle of תשלומין decides who can still bring a festival offering after the first day. It also defends עולא's choice not to make the person טמא מת.

phrases.english: Ulla holds:
all of them (the festival days) are make-up days for the first day.
phrases.notes: The later days are not new obligations. They only complete the first day's obligation.

phrases.english: One who is fit on the first day is fit on all of them,
and whenever one is not fit on the first day,
he is not fit on any of them.
phrases.notes: So a טמא מת on day one loses his חגיגה for the whole festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 21 that a טמא מת could bring his חגיגה later in the festival.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces an underlying principle (תשלומין) held by עולא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A טמא מת could bring his חגיגה on the seventh day, after becoming pure.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because all the days are תשלומין of the first, someone unfit on the first day can never bring his חגיגה. So making him טמא מת would cause a total loss.

steps.title: רב נחמן says עולא's plan is impractical
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן sends a message to עולא: who would ever agree to pull up his tent and run far away just to change the count?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to them: Go and tell עולא: who will listen and pull out his tent pegs and his tent and run off?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks עולא's whole idea of sending a person away on a distant journey. He says no one would actually do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a challenge to עולא's logic. It is a practical objection. Even if the plan works on paper, no real person will pack up his tent and leave Jerusalem on פסח just to fix the numbers. That makes the plan useless.

keyTerms.meaning: Go and say to him
Listens / obeys
His tent pegs
His tent / dwelling
Runs

steps.whatToRemember: עולא's solution may work in theory, but רב נחמן rejects it as unrealistic. No one will uproot himself and run away on פסח.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said to them (the students):
Go and say to Ulla:
Who will listen (to you)
to uproot his tent pegs and his tent and run off?
phrases.notes: A vivid picture of how unrealistic it is to send someone far away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After עולא's method was defended in theory, רב נחמן rejects it on practical grounds.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's solution of sending a person away on a distant journey
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A solution that no person will actually carry out is not a real solution.

steps.title: רב's ruling when most are זבין and a minority are טמאי מתים
steps.stepSummary: A new case: most of the people are זבין and a minority are טמאי מתים. רב rules that the טמאי מתים do not bring the פסח, neither on the first פסח nor on פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: If most of them were זבין and a minority were טמאי מתים, רב said: those טמאי מתים do not bring the פסח, not on the first and not on the second.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion with a new case and gives רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זבין can never bring the פסח while impure, even when they are the majority. So in this case the community does not bring the first פסח at all. The surprise is רב's ruling that the טמאי מתים lose פסח שני too, even though a טמא מת normally does bring פסח שני.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces an אמוראי discussion)
People impure from a bodily discharge (זב)
People impure from contact with a dead body
The second פסח, a month later, for those who missed the first

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume that a majority of impure people always means the פסח is brought in impurity. That rule is for טמאי מתים. זבין, whose impurity comes from their own body, never bring it while impure.

phrases.english: It was stated: If the majority of them were zavim,
and a minority of them were impure from a corpse,
Rav said: those who are impure from a corpse

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָן עוֹשִׂין לֹא בָּרִאשׁוֹן וְלֹא בַּשֵּׁנִי.
phrases.english: do not perform the Pesaḥ, not on the first and not on the second.
phrases.notes: They lose both the first פסח and פסח שני.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic after the עולא discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When most of the people are זבין and a minority are טמאי מתים, the טמאי מתים bring neither the first פסח nor פסח שני.

steps.title: Why the טמאי מתים lose both the first and second פסח
steps.stepSummary: On the first פסח they cannot bring it, because they are a minority and a minority cannot bring it while impure. On פסח שני they cannot bring it either, because individuals bring פסח שני only when the community brought the first פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the first they do not bring it, because they are a minority, and a minority does not bring it on the first. On the second they also do not bring it. Wherever the community brings it on the first, the individual brings it on the second. Wherever the community does not bring it on the first, the individual does not bring it on the second.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רב's ruling, one part at a time: first why they lose the first פסח, then why they lose פסח שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part is simple: only a majority of טמאי מתים may bring the פסח while impure, and these are only a minority. The new idea is the second part. פסח שני depends on the community having brought the first פסח. Here the majority were זבין, so the community did not bring the first פסח, and individuals get no פסח שני.

keyTerms.meaning: A minority
The community (as a whole)
An individual
They perform / bring (the offering)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, פסח שני is tied to the community. An individual brings פסח שני only if the community brought the first פסח. If the community did not bring it, there is no פסח שני for the individual.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that פסח שני is not simply a personal second chance. It depends on what the community did on the first פסח.

phrases.english: On the first they do not perform it, because they are the minority,
and the minority does not perform it on the first (while impure).
On the second they also do not perform it,
because whenever the community performs it on the first,
the individual performs it on the second.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּלָא עָבְדִי צִיבּוּר בָּרִאשׁוֹן —
phrases.english: Whenever the community does not perform it on the first,
the individual does not perform it on the second.
phrases.notes: Here the majority were זבין, so the community did not bring it. That is why the טמאי מתים lose פסח שני.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רב's ruling in Step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Individuals bring פסח שני only when the community brought the first פסח. A minority of טמאי מתים does not bring the פסח on the first while impure.

steps.title: שמואל challenges רב from the verse 'in its appointed time'
steps.stepSummary: שמואל sends a message to רב asking how he explains the פָּסוּק that requires the פסח to be brought בְּמוֹעֲדוֹ, in its set time.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to them: Go and say to אבא (רב): What do you do with the verse 'Let בני ישראל offer the פסח in its appointed time'?
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל attacks רב's ruling from step 24 that the minority of טמאי מתים bring no פסח at all. He uses a פָּסוּק that says the פסח must be brought in its proper time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בְּמוֹעֲדוֹ teaches that the פסח must be brought on its day, even in טומאה if necessary. Under רב's ruling, no one brings a פסח on the first פסח, which seems to contradict this verse. שמואל suggests the טמאי מתים should bring it in טומאה on the first פסח rather than skip it entirely.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who often argues with רב
רב's personal name (אבא אריכא)
In its appointed time; the פסח must be brought on its day
What do you do with it? How do you explain this source?

steps.confusionAlert: 'אבא' here does not mean 'father.' It is רב's actual name, so שמואל is sending the question to רב himself.

phrases.english: Shmuel said to them,
phrases.notes: To the messengers who reported רב's ruling

phrases.english: Go and say to Abba (Rav):
'Let the children of Israel offer the Paschal lamb in its appointed time'
phrases.notes: במדבר ט:ב

phrases.english: what do you do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling that the minority of טמאי מתים bring no פסח at all
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the טמאי מתים bring no פסח, neither on the first פסח nor on פסח שני
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse בְּמוֹעֲדוֹ requires the פסח to be offered on its day, but רב's ruling leaves it completely unoffered.

steps.title: רב answers: what is impossible is impossible
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that if all the people were זבין, no פסח could be brought either. So when it cannot be done, it cannot be done, and our case is the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to them: Go and say to him: When they are all זבין, what do you do with the verse? Rather, since it is impossible, it is impossible. Here too, it is impossible.
steps.whatsHappening: רב defends his ruling. He points out that even שמואל must agree the verse is not kept when everyone is a זב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב can never bring the פסח in טומאה, so if the whole nation were זבין, nobody could bring it, verse or no verse. That proves the verse only applies when bringing the פסח is possible. In רב's case, it is not possible, because the minority cannot bring it in טומאה. So the verse does not force anything.

keyTerms.meaning: People with a זיבה discharge, whose טומאה is never pushed aside for the פסח
Since it is impossible
Here too; applying the same logic to our case

steps.whatToRemember: רב's principle: the requirement of בְּמוֹעֲדוֹ only applies where bringing the פסח is possible. When the law makes it impossible, the פסח is simply not brought.

phrases.english: He (Rav) said to them, go and say to him:
when they are all zavim
what do you do with it?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כֵּיוָן דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר — לָא אֶפְשָׁר.
phrases.english: Rather, since it is impossible, it is impossible.
Here too, it is impossible.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲווֹ כּוּלְּהוּ זָבִין מַאי עָבְדַתְּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers שמואל's challenge with a counter-case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-question showing the verse cannot apply where fulfilling it is impossible
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse בְּמוֹעֲדוֹ demands that the פסח be brought on its day no matter what
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse applies only when it is possible. When the law prevents it, as with all זבין or with רב's case, the פסח is not brought.

steps.title: New case: most are impure from a corpse, a minority are זבין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces the reverse case: most of the people are טמאי מתים and a minority are זבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: If most of them were טמאי מתים and a minority of them were זבין,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new case for an argument between אמוראים that comes in the next step. Here the majority are טמאי מתים, so the community brings the פסח in טומאה, but the זבין cannot join.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When most of the community is טמא מת, the פסח is brought on the first פסח even in טומאה. A זב's טומאה is never pushed aside, so the minority of זבין are left out. The question will be whether these זבין, once pure, can make it up on פסח שני.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated; introduces a dispute between אמוראים
The majority of them
The minority of them

steps.confusionAlert: This is the opposite of רב's case in step 24. There, most were זבין. Here, most are טמאי מתים, so the community does bring the פסח on the first פסח.

phrases.english: It was stated: If most of them were impure from a corpse
and a minority of them were zavim,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: הָיוּ רוּבָּן טְמֵאֵי מֵתִים וּמִיעוּטָן זָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces the reverse of רב's case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case setup: majority טמאי מתים and minority זבין. The ruling follows in the next step.

steps.title: רב הונא and רב אדא בר אהבה argue about a make-up
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says a פסח brought in טומאה has no make-up, so the זבין do not bring פסח שני. רב אדא בר אהבה says it does have a make-up, so the זבין bring פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: There is no make-up for a פסח that is brought in טומאה. And רב אדא בר אהבה said: There is a make-up for a פסח that is brought in טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים argue about the case from the last step. The question is whether the זבין, who missed the community's impure פסח, can bring their own on פסח שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסח שני is a make-up (תשלומין) for those who missed the first פסח. רב הונא holds that once the community brought its פסח in טומאה, there is no make-up. רב אדא בר אהבה holds that the make-up still applies, so the זבין, once pure, bring פסח שני.

keyTerms.meaning: אמורא, student of רב
אמורא who disagrees with רב הונא here
A make-up; here, פסח שני as a make-up for the first פסח
A פסח offered while the community is impure

steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute decides whether פסח שני exists at all in a year when the community brought its פסח in טומאה.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
There is no make-up for a Paschal lamb brought in impurity,
and Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
There is a make-up for a Paschal lamb brought in impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: אֵין תַּשְׁלוּמִין לְפֶסַח הַבָּא בְּטוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two rulings on the case just set up
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: no פסח שני after a פסח brought in טומאה. רב אדא בר אהבה: there is פסח שני.

steps.title: Suggested root of the argument: impurity is only pushed aside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב הונא, who says there is no make-up, holds that טומאה is only 'pushed aside' (דחויה) for the community, not fully permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that they disagree about this: the one who says there is no make-up for a פסח brought in טומאה holds that טומאה is only pushed aside for the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins proposing the deeper reason behind the argument. It explains רב הונא's side here and is setting up the explanation of רב אדא בר אהבה's side, which comes in step 31.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If טומאה is only דחויה, the impure פסח is a second-best exception, not a normal פסח. So we cannot learn from it that people who missed it get a make-up on פסח שני. Step 31 gives the opposite view, that טומאה is fully permitted (הותרה), as the basis for רב אדא בר אהבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say they argue about this? A proposed root of the dispute
He holds
For the community, טומאה is only pushed aside, not fully permitted

steps.confusionAlert: 'דחויה' does not mean the טומאה stops mattering. It means it is set aside only out of necessity, but remains a problem wherever it can be avoided.

phrases.english: Shall we say that they disagree about this,

phrases.aramaic: דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר: אֵין תַּשְׁלוּמִין לְפֶסַח הַבָּא בְּטוּמְאָה,
phrases.english: that the one who says: There is no make-up for a Paschal lamb brought in impurity,
holds: Impurity is overridden (only pushed aside) for the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes the conceptual root of the רב הונא / רב אדא בר אהבה dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proposal: רב הונא's view (no make-up) rests on the idea that טומאה is only דחויה בציבור. Step 31 gives the other half of the proposal.

steps.title: The other side of the proposal: רב אדא בר אהבה holds טומאה is fully permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its suggestion. The one who says there is a make-up (רב אדא בר אהבה) must hold that טומאה הותרה בציבור, meaning טומאה is fully permitted for the community.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who says a פסח brought in טומאה does have a make-up holds that טומאה is fully permitted for the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the suggestion it started in step 30. Now it explains רב אדא בר אהבה's side, the opposite of רב הונא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If טומאה is fully permitted for the community, then the community's פסח counts as a normal, proper first פסח. So the minority זבין, who could not join it, are just like individuals who missed the first פסח. That is why they bring פסח שני as a make-up. This sets up a neat split: רב הונא holds דחויה, and רב אדא בר אהבה holds הותרה.

keyTerms.meaning: A make-up. Here it means פסח שני, which is brought by people who missed the first פסח.
Was fully permitted. The prohibition is removed completely.
The community, here the majority of the Jewish people.
He holds. It introduces the reason behind someone's view.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two words. הוּתְּרָה means 'fully permitted', as if there were no problem at all. דְּחוּיָה means 'pushed aside': the problem still exists, but it gives way because of the community's need.

phrases.english: And the one who says: there is a make-up
phrases.notes: This refers to רב אדא בר אהבה from step 29.

phrases.english: for a פסח that is brought in impurity,
holds: impurity is fully permitted for the community.
phrases.notes: This is the mirror image of רב הונא's view in step 30.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר: יֵשׁ תַּשְׁלוּמִין לְפֶסַח הַבָּא בְּטוּמְאָה, קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This completes the two-sided proposal begun in step 30. It assigns the opposite principle to the other אמורא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The proposal says that רב אדא בר אהבה, who holds there is a make-up, believes טומאה הותרה בציבור.

steps.title: Rejection: both hold טומאה is only pushed aside, and they argue about something else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says 'No.' Everyone agrees that טומאה דחויה בציבור. The argument between רב הונא and רב אדא בר אהבה is about a different point. The גמרא begins to explain it with 'This Master holds —'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: No. Everyone agrees that impurity is only pushed aside for the community. They argue about this: This Master holds —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the explanation from steps 30 and 31. It then starts setting up a new explanation of the argument, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proposal said the argument depended on הותרה versus דחויה. The גמרא now says that is not necessary, because both אמוראים can agree that טומאה is only דחויה. So the argument must come from a different reason. The words 'מר סבר' open the explanation of רב הונא's side, but the explanation itself comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: They say: no. This formula rejects a suggestion that was just made.
Everyone agrees. Both sides of the argument hold this.
Pushed aside. The prohibition still exists, but it gives way for the community.
About this they argue. It introduces the true point of the argument.
This Master holds. Here it refers to רב הונא.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא. It tries to tie an argument to a big principle, then shows the argument can work even if both sides agree on that principle. This keeps each אמורא from being forced into a larger position.

phrases.english: They say: No.
phrases.notes: This rejects the proposal from steps 30 and 31.

phrases.english: Everyone agrees that impurity is only pushed aside for the community,
and about this they argue:
This Master holds —
phrases.notes: This refers to רב הונא. The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This rejects the proposed link between the argument and הותרה versus דחויה. It opens a new explanation of the argument.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The rejection applies to the claim that רב הונא and רב אדא בר אהבה argue because one holds דחויה and the other holds הותרה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proposal is not necessary. The argument can be explained even if both agree that טומאה is only דחויה בציבור, so it must come from a different point.
